reading_for_voided_daf_grant: [I] A grant check is a gratuitous transfer, so §1005(c)(6) lets the sponsor rebut the presumption; a documented 90-day void also fits §1005(c)(8). A booked "grants payable" record is still prima facie evidence under §1005(a), so the sponsor carries the burden.
key_quote: or other business entity, whether or not for profit … (6) issued without consideration … (8) voided [not later than 90 days] [within a reasonable time] after issuance for a valid business reason set forth in a contemporaneous record
notes: §1005(a): a holder record of an unpaid debt is prima facie evidence. Priority: §302 (owner last-known address) then §304 (holder domicile if owner state does not provide for custodial taking).

reading_for_voided_daf_grant: [I] A DAF grant check is not payment for goods or services, so §1315(1-a) may not reach it. If New York does not provide for custodial taking, RUUPA-style §304 rules in the holder's domicile state could apply instead.
key_quote: Any amount representing outstanding checks issued on and after July first, nineteen hundred seventy-four in payment for goods or for services
notes: Other §1315 subdivisions (gift certificates, escrow, lottery, state checks) do not fit grant checks.

reading_for_voided_daf_grant: [I] A covered check held "in the ordinary course of the person's business" for three years is presumed abandoned. Whether a sponsor that has voided the check and returned the funds to the DAF still "owes" the charity is not addressed.

notes: CJP (DAF policy PDF lists a Boston address) is a Massachusetts holder; holder domicile matters only under second-priority rules [I].

reading_for_voided_daf_grant: [I] A charity cannot enforce an uncashed DAF grant check against the sponsor-drawer, because the check was issued without consideration. That supports the view that no "fixed and certain" obligation is owed to the payee.

notes: A holder in due course takes free of this defense; a payee charity normally is not a holder in due course against its own drawer [I].
